BATCH F · BOARD 6 OF 6

Draft to preprint, rights-checked

1 → 2 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 8 → 9. Seven steps across five months. The measure is not speed — a paper takes as long as the science takes — it is that nothing has to be reconstructed at the end: the data statement, the CRediT roles, the checklist and the rights position all exist already, because each was recorded when it was true.

WHAT WAS NEVER RE-CREATED AT THE END
Data availability — written at step 1, when the figure was bound to DS-1174.
Code availability — the version and DOI of gate-and-quantify, from the repository.
CRediT statement — roles recorded as the work happened, confirmed by each author.
Funding and ethics — from the grant and ethics records, with the right award numbers.
Reporting checklist — 17 of 21 items linked to paragraphs, not ticked from memory.
WHERE THE FLOW CAN STOP
Only at step 6. Outcome A continues to step 8 the same day. Outcome B routes to private hosting with request-a-copy and the preprint still goes up, because the submitted version is separately permitted. Outcome C uploads now and releases on a scheduled date. In none of the three does a researcher end up holding a file they are not allowed to hold.
THE STEP THAT PAYS FOR THE REST
Step 5. The objection that would have cost a rejection at eLife arrives in week 11 from a colleague, not in month 9 from a reviewer. Every other step in this ribbon saves minutes; that one saves a submission cycle — and a submission cycle in this field is four to five months.
